cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: I haven’t seen you for a bit, Marie.

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: No. I’ve been busy with my project.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: You’re making a vegan alternative to eggs, aren’t you? Something that doesn’t use animal products?

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: Yes. I’m using chickpeas. I had two main aims when I first started looking for an alternative to eggs, but actually I’ve found chickpeas have got more advantages.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: But how about your project on reusing waste food – you were looking at bread, weren’t you?

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yes. It’s been hard work, but I’ve enjoyed it. The basic process was quite straightforward – breaking the stale bread down to a paste then reforming it.

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: But you were using 3-D printing, weren’t you, to make the paste into biscuits?

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yeah, I’d used that before, but in this project, I had time to play around with different patterns for the biscuits and finding how I could add fruit and vegetables to make them a more appetising colour, and I was really pleased with what I managed to produce. Q21/22

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: It must’ve been a great feeling to make something appetising out of bits of old bread that would’ve been thrown away otherwise. Q21/22

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: It was. And I’m hoping that some of the restaurants in town will be interested in the biscuits. I’m going to send them some samples.

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: I came across something on the internet yesterday that might interest you. It was a company that’s developed touch-sensitive sensors for food labels.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Mmm?

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: It’s a special sort of label on the food package. When the label’s smooth, the food is fresh and then when you can feel bumps on the label, that means the food’s gone bad. It started off as a project to help visually impaired people know whether food was fit to eat or not.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Interesting. So just solid food?

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: No, things like milk and juice as well. But actually, I thought it might be really good for drug storage in hospitals and pharmacies. Q23/24

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Right. And coming back to food, maybe it’d be possible to use it for other things besides freshness. Like how many kilograms a joint of meat is. for example. Q23/24

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: Yes, there’s all sorts of possibilities.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: I was reading an article about food trends predicting how eating habits might change in the next few years.

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: Oh – things like more focus on local products? That seems so obvious, but the shops are still full of imported foods. Q25

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yes, they need to be more proactive to address that.

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: And somehow motivate consumers to change, yes.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: One thing everyone’s aware of is the need for a reduction in unnecessary packaging – but just about everything you buy in supermarkets is still covered in plastic. The government needs to do something about it. Q26

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: Absolutely. It’s got to change.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Do you think there’ll be more interest in gluten – and lactose-free food?

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: For people with allergies or food intolerances? I don’t know. Lots of people I know have been buying that type of food for years now. Q27

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yes, even if they haven’t been diagnosed with an allergy.

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: That’s right. One thing I ’ve noticed is the number of branded products related to celebrity chefs – people watch them cooking on TV and then buy things like spice mixes or frozen foods with the chef’s name on . . . I bought something like that once, but I won’t again. Q28

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yeah – I bought a ready-made spice mix for chicken which was supposed to be used by a chef I’d seen on television, and it didn’t actually taste of anything.

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: Mm. Did the article mention ‘ghost kitchens’ used to produce takeaway food?

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: No. What are they?

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: Well, they might have the name of a restaurant, but actually they’re a cooking facility just for delivery meals – the public don’t ever go there. But people aren’t aware of that – it’s all kept very quiet. Q29

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: So people don’t realise the food’s not actually from the restaurant?

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Did you know more and more people are using all sorts of different mushrooms now, to treat different health concerns? Things like heart problems?

cues.speaker: MARIE
cues.text: Hmm. They might be taking a big risk there. Q30

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yes, it’s hard to know which varieties are safe to eat. Anyway maybe now…
